author: Meredith Dean
description:
In rural America, guns are a fact of life. But even conservatives agree that properly locking them up is crucial in preventing deaths

I have six guns in my house.

The first was a vintage Winchester 12-gauge. It was the winter of 1990, and my husband and I had just moved from an urban block in north-west Philadelphia to 100-year-old farmhouse in Appalachian Virginia, where my family goes back seven generations.

Continue reading...
title: I own six guns. Here’s how to talk to conservatives about firearms

author: Rachel Savage in Sharpeville
description:
Claim relating to infamous apartheid-era shooting of protesters part of wave of litigation for apartheid-era crimes

The day dawned brightly on 21 March 1960, as residents of the South African township of Sharpeville gathered to protest against pass laws, which forced “Black, Indian and Coloured” South Africans to carry documents at all times specifying where they were allowed to be.

Abraham Mofokeng joined the march, one of dozens organised nationwide by the Pan Africanist Congress (PAC), a breakaway group from the African National Congress. “The weather was very nice, the sun was out. You could not have suspected that the day would go so horribly,” said Mofokeng, who was then a 20-year-old factory worker.

Continue reading...
title: Victims sue South African government over 1961 Sharpeville massacre that left 91 dead

author: Tom Ambrose
description:
Maryland judge issues preliminary injunction blocking Trump’s executive order targeting what he termed ‘birth tourism’

Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.

A US federal judge has blocked the Trump administration from enforcing a new executive order limiting who qualifies for birthright citizenship.

House Democrats rejected a constitutional amendment proposed by Republicans to ensure the size of the supreme court is permanently capped at nine justices. The proposal, a Republican effort to make the supreme court a campaign issue ahead of the November midterms, failed 212-206.

House Democratic lawmakers introduced a war powers resolution seeking to stop the Trump administration’s boat strikes. Gregory W Meeks, Adam Smith, Jim Himes and Bennie G Thompson said people have been killed “without due process” in attacks never authorized by Congress.

Senator Richard Blument
title: Judge blocks new Trump bid against birthright citizenship – US politics live

author: Emily Halnon
description:
At this week’s world championship, the women’s record holder who once feared a 5K will try to top her own 144-hour distance – and beat the US men’s mark

While many teachers head back to school this week, middle-school math teacher Megan Eckert will be 5,000 miles from her classroom in Santa Fe, New Mexico. She has a good reason to miss a few classes: she’ll be competing at the Global Organization of Multi-Day Ultramarathoners World Championship.

On Thursday, more than 100 runners will gather on a start line in Balatonfüred, Hungary, and attempt to run as many miles as they can in six days.

Continue reading...
title: 606 miles in six days: teacher Megan Eckert chases ultrarunning history – and a men’s record

author: Alexandra Villarreal in New York
description:
Trump administration has indefinitely stranded hundreds of kids and lawyers from over 50 organizations are fighting for their release

An army of attorneys is rallying to free hundreds of children from immigration custody, where they have been stranded indefinitely by the Trump administration without their parents or loved ones, the Guardian can reveal.

The effort is a counter strike to what critics see as unprecedented moves by federal officials to ride roughshod over children’s rights and increase deportations – while in the meantime corralling them in conditions that can allegedly lead to psychological harm.

Continue read
title: Revealed: US attorneys rally to free children held in immigration custody

author: Juan A Ramírez
description:
In an ambitious new project, a cast of New Yorkers will help to create a one-of-a-kind tribute to New York City on stage in Central Park

Last year, theatre-makers Emily Lim and Dan Canham spent time in Sunderland developing a three-night live performance that sought to capture the north-east city’s essence and history through music, dance and spoken word. It was Lim’s final coup as the director of the National Theatre’s now defunct, UK-wide community programme, Public Arts, and the result was Public Record – a title that nods to both physical media (the audio is stored at the British Library and Sunderland Museum) and to the institutional archive.

“It’s very full-circle,” Lim says, now doing the same for New York City’s Public Theatre, whose own Public Works branch inspired the National’s initiative. “The key difference is that instead of serving the country and national profile, our responsibility here is to serve the city.”
title: ‘The myth is constantly being told’: creating a live album on stage as tribute to New York

author: Jakub Krupa
description:
Around 70,000 irregular migrants crossed into the north African territory of Ceuta from Morocco in August

Sánchez begins by paying tribute to the people of Ceuta, “who are enduring difficult times” as a result of the crisis.

He also reaffirms Spain’s sovereignty over Ceuta and Melilla.

Continue reading...
title: Thousands protest over Spain’s handling of Ceuta border crisis – Europe live

author: Mark Brown North of England correspondent
description:
Visitors to Nostell in West Yorkshire will get to see cutting-edge research into work considered the only faithful copy of Holbein masterpiece

A spectacular, internationally important painting of Thomas More and his family is to have its secrets explored as the public look on.

The open heritage science project, scheduled to begin on Thursday, is a UK first and will deploy techniques used at the Rijksmuseum in Amsterdam during its famous public restoration of Rembrandt’s masterpiece The Night Watch.

Continue reading...
title: Public given rare access as Thomas More painting goes under microscope

author: Kate Ravilious
description:
El Niño is associated with weaker monsoons in India – but research suggests it can also bring more extreme rainfall

The world is bracing for a “super” El Niño, and its effects are already being felt in India, where the monsoon has brought less rain than average but more intense downpours.

Meteorologists predict that the current El Niño, which is developing over the Pacific, could be one of the strongest in living memory. India is likely to be heavily affected, particularly later in the monsoon, when El Niño’s influence tends to strengthen.

Continue reading...
title: Why El Niño can mean less rain but heavier downpours for India

author: Presented by Helen Pidd with John Kampfner, produced by Tom Glasser and Brian McNamara; executive producer Homa Khaleeli
description:
Ulrich Siegmund, the charismatic young leader of the AfD party in Saxony-Anhalt, has been labelled Germany’s most dangerous man by Der Spiegel. John Kampfner explains why

The German news magazine Der Spiegel has long had a taste for provocation. But one of its cover stories last month really captured people’s attention. It carried a picture of a young east German politician called Ulrich Siegmund. He looked pretty good, his chin covered with designer stubble, his hair combed into a neat quiff, his green eyes staring right into the camera, under the headline “Der gefährlichste Mann Deutschlands”: Germany’s most dangerous man.

You might think Siegmund would hate that Spiegel cover. Far from it. On the campaign trail in recent weeks he has been autographing copies: he even filmed himself signing one for his 800,000 TikTok followers. If the polls are correct, Siegmund could soon become the first far-right leader of a German state since Adolf Hitler
title: Is Ulrich Siegmund the most dangerous man in Germany? - podcast
